diagram_math_checks.result: q:E->E/G is the original orbit map; U is the open neighbourhood of step 1.1; V=q(U). The upper map g|_U has domain U and codomain gU, with inverse restriction of g^{-1}; the lower maps have domains U and gU and common codomain V. This follows from F1, F2 and steps 1.1-2.1, checked against def-covering-space-action and def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods.

For every x in U, q(g.x)=q(x) because gx and x lie in the same orbit; hence q|_{gU} composed with g|_U equals q|_U. The drawn arrows are U to gU (right), U to V (down-right), and gU to V (down-left), exactly these domains/codomains. No reverse or additional arrow is asserted.

By F1, distinct translates are disjoint and each action map is a homeomorphism. The quotient map is open since q^{-1}(q(O)) is the union of translates of every open O; its restriction to U is injective since a nonidentity translate cannot meet U, and it is onto V by definition. The same holds for gU. These justify the three homeomorphisms of step 2.1. q^{-1}(V) is the disjoint union indexed by all g in G (step 1.1). The triangle compares U and gU and does not assert finite degree; when g=1 its two upper objects denote the same sheet and the horizontal map is identity.

The original Statement, Facts and all five proof steps are byte-identical to the frozen source. No figure-based deck-group assertion or new hypothesis was added. F4/F5 and step 4.1 retain the original independent one-point-determination argument; local deck definitions and the actual proposition interface were read. The rigorous proof remains independent of the triangle.
